case_title: State of Gujarat & Anr. v. Narayan @ Narayan Sai @ Mot a Bhagwan
previous_criminal_record: Yes, engaged in illegal activities inside the jail, attempted to bribe public officials, threatened and assaulted witnesses
aggravating_circumstances: Criminal misconduct to hinder judicial proceedings, threats to witnesses, mass following of followers willing to commit offences, illegal activities in jail
mitigating_circumstances: Released on furlough for mother's health, no illegal activity reported since release
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment with fine
neutral_facts: The accused was convicted of multiple offences including rape and cruelty. During the trial, there were attempts to bribe public officials and threaten witnesses. The accused was released on furlough for a period of fourteen days. The authorities denied the furlough due to concerns about public peace and the accused's criminal history. The accused had a mass following of followers who were willing to commit offences at his instance. The accused was released on furlough in December 2020 for his mother's health and was granted interim bail. The accused was not involved in any illegal activities during the period of furlough. The High Court allowed the furlough leave, but the Supreme Court overturned this decision, stating that the furlough should not be granted due to the accused's criminal conduct and the threat to public peace.
